topics.title: Combine and split shapes: Create 2D shapes from combining and splitting common shapes; quadrilaterals

questions.stem: Count the sides and inspect the angles of this 2D shape. What is its name, and is it regular or irregular?
questions.hint: First count the number of straight sides (3=triangle, 4=quadrilateral, 5=pentagon, 6=hexagon, 7=heptagon, 8=octagon, 9=nonagon), then check if ALL sides and ALL angles are equal.

keyPoints.note: The number of straight sides determines the polygon name.
Regular = all sides equal AND all angles equal; otherwise irregular.

steps.explain: Number each straight side around the outside of the shape. There are \(3\) sides in total.

steps.explain: Match \(3\) sides to the polygon word bank: a \(3\)-sided shape is called a triangle.
Compare all \(3\) side lengths and all \(3\) interior angles. Every side has the same length (marked with equal ticks) and every angle has the same size, so the shape is regular.
steps.work: \(\text{All sides equal and all angles equal} \Rightarrow \text{regular}\)

questions.stem: In the classic "Join the dots" puzzle, you join all \(9\) dots using \(4\) straight lines without lifting your pencil or going over any line twice. What kind of shape do the \(4\) lines form?
options: A right-angled triangle with an arrow tail (arrow shape)
questions.hint: Think outside the box! Two of the lines must extend PAST the outer dots so they turn sharply and cover the remaining dots, forming a big triangle with a diagonal line inside.

keyPoints.note: Extending lines outside the 3×3 square is the key to solving the 9-dot puzzle.

steps.explain: Line 1 (blue): Start at the top-left dot and draw horizontally across the top row, extending ONE unit PAST the top-right dot.
steps.work: \(\text{Line 1 covers 3 top dots and extends outside}\)

questions.stem: Which of these shapes (A, B, or C) is an irregular quadrilateral?
options: Both Shape A and Shape C
questions.hint: A quadrilateral has 4 sides, and "irregular" means its sides and angles are NOT all equal.

keyPoints.note: Must have 4 sides, with unequal side lengths/angles.

steps.explain: Check Shape A: it is a square with 4 equal sides and 4 equal right angles, so it is a REGULAR quadrilateral.
Check Shape B: count its sides — it has 6 sides, so it is an irregular hexagon (not a quadrilateral).
Check Shape C: it has 4 straight sides of different lengths and different angles, so it is an irregular quadrilateral.

questions.stem: The red dashed line is a vertical line of symmetry. In Row 1, the three left squares (from left to right) are Green, Red, Yellow. What colours must go in the three right squares of Row 1 (from left to right) to make the pattern symmetrical?
questions.hint: A line of symmetry acts like a mirror! The square closest to the red line (Yellow) must reflect directly across to be closest to the red line on the right.

keyPoints.note: Mirror reflection reverses the left-to-right order of colours.

steps.explain: Look at Row 1 on the left of the red symmetry line: moving outward from the line, the colours are Yellow, then Red, then Green.
Reflect each square across the red mirror line: the square immediately to the right of the line must match Yellow.

questions.stem: In the 4×4 Coloured Squares Puzzle, you use red, blue, green, and yellow tiles so that NO two tiles of the same colour share an edge (touch horizontally or vertically). If a square touches a Red tile on its left, a Blue tile above it, and a Green tile on its right, what colour MUST that square be?
questions.hint: Eliminate the three colours already touching that square (Red, Blue, Green). Only one colour from the four remains!

keyPoints.text: NO two tiles of the same colour share an edge
keyPoints.note: Check all neighbouring squares to eliminate forbidden colours.

steps.explain: List the four available tile colours: Red, Blue, Green, and Yellow.
Eliminate the colours of the three touching neighbours: Red (left), Blue (above), and Green (right).
The only remaining legal colour is Yellow.
Therefore, the square MUST be coloured Yellow.

topics.title: Area — grid structure: Measure areas of shapes and irregular shapes using a grid; compare surfaces using metric units

questions.stem: Use the areas of Shapes A, B, C, and D to answer: Which shape has the largest area?
questions.hint: Find the area of every rectangle first by multiplying rows × columns: A = 4×3 = 12, B = 2×3 = 6, C = 8×1 = 8, D = 6×3 = 18.

keyPoints.text: areas of Shapes A, B, C, and D
keyPoints.note: Count squares (rows × columns): A = 12, B = 6, C = 8, D = 18.

steps.explain: Count the squares inside each shape by multiplying columns by rows: A = \(4 \times 3 = 12\), B = \(2 \times 3 = 6\), C = \(8 \times 1 = 8\), D = \(6 \times 3 = 18\).
